blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The abstract and Sec. 1 state the dataset (PS-SPLIT; 79K bird images from 257 real taxonomic splits with 257 matched controls), the new task (discovery by category splitting), the four adapted GCD baselines, and the transformer K-estimator; all of these are evaluated in Sec. 6 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Sec. 7 is a dedicated Limitations and Discussion section covering multiple limitations: visual-only assumption, birds-only restriction, K max = 2 K_{\max}=2 (two-way splits only), citizen-science biases, control matching being taxonomic rather than ecological, and splitting-only scope. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper presents an empirical benchmark with adapted baselines and contains no theoretical results or proofs. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The dataset construction pipeline is fully described in Sec. 3 and Appendix D . Backbones (DINOv1, DINOv2 with registers, GCD, SimGCD, UNO+, SelEx, SINR) and the K-estimation / clustering methods are described in Sec. 5 with citations to the original implementations; the transformer K-estimator architecture, losses, optimiser, and training schedule are given in Appendix E . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Sec. 3 the dataset and code (including the construction pipeline and the K-estimator implementations) will be released Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Sec. 5 describes backbones, geographic encoder, K-estimation methods, and clustering choices; the 50/50 known/novel coarse-class protocol is given in Sec. 4 ; full transformer architecture and training hyperparameters (SGD with momentum 0.9, learning rate 0.1, 50 epochs, 5-head ensemble, λ = 0.3 \lambda=0.3 , τ = 0.07 \tau=0.07 , K max = 2 K_{\max}=2 ) are provided in Appendix E . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [No] Justification: Results are reported from a single training seed for each fine-tuned backbone; we did not run multi-seed experiments for the full backbone × \times K-estimation grid due to compute cost. Many category discovery papers report results from previous category discovery papers without reimplementing as training each approach can take multiple days per dataset depending on compute available. As we are introducing a new task and dataset, each backbone needed to be trained for each dataset and task, limiting the runs that were feasible. We will add error bars in a future revision. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix E reports that the transformer K-estimator trains in roughly ten minutes on a single A6000 GPU on full PS-SPLIT (assuming precomputed backbone features) and less on PS-SPLIT-Small. Backbone fine-tuning compute follows the original publications cited in Sec. 5 ; all reported runs used a single A6000 GPU. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The work conforms with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. The dataset is built only from research-grade iNaturalist observations whose licences permit redistribution for research; no human subjects are involved; Sec. 7 discusses appropriate use and the role of expert and genetic confirmation when methods evaluated on PS-SPLIT are applied in practice. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Sec. 1 motivates the work as supporting biodiversity monitoring and species discovery (positive impact). Sec. 7 discusses potential misuse: methods evaluated on PS-SPLIT should propose candidate splits for downstream expert review and genetic confirmation, not be used as a substitute for taxonomic decisions, and the dataset inherits known geographic and taxonomic biases that could affect deployment. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: PS-SPLIT comprises research-grade citizen-science bird images released under licences that permit redistribution for research; it does not contain personal data, generative-model outputs, or content with high risk of misuse, so no special safeguards are required for release. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All cited assets are credited at point of use: iNaturalist research-grade observations [ 24 ] (only those whose licences permit redistribution for research are included); MegaDetector v5 [ 3 ] ; Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct [ 2 ] ; DINOv1 [ 8 ] ; DINOv2 with registers [ 36 , 15 ] ; SINR [ 14 ] ; GCD [ 52 ] ; SimGCD [ 55 ] ; UNO+ [ 18 ] ; SelEx [ 40 ] ; CUB-200-2011 [ 54 ] ; Stanford Cars [ 26 ] ; FGVC Aircraft [ 32 ] . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: PS-SPLIT is the new asset. Sec. 3 provides headline statistics, the construction pipeline summary, and a comparison with existing fine-grained benchmarks; Appendix D contains the full construction pipeline; Appendix H describes the supplementary per-species JSON release (taxon IDs, binomial nomenclature, splitting/control type, image counts); a datasheet, hosting plan, and licensing details accompany the submission as supplementary material. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing or research with human subjects. The underlying iNaturalist observations were contributed by volunteer naturalists for biodiversity science independently of and prior to this work; we use only the resulting research-grade images and associated metadata under their existing redistribution-permitting licences. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The work does not involve human-subjects research and therefore does not require IRB approval. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct [ 2 ] is used as a vision–language quality reviewer in stage four of the dataset-construction pipeline ( Sec. 3 , Appendix D ); it scores seven binary quality criteria per image and assigns a coarse pose label, with intra-split pose consistency enforced. The full prompt template is reproduced in the appendix. No LLMs are used in the methods being benchmarked. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 抽象和Sec. 1说明了数据集(PS-SPLIT;来自257个真实分类分出并配有257个匹配控件的79K鸟类图像),新任务(通过分类分出来发现),四个经过改造的GCD基线,以及变压器K-估测器;所有这些都用Sec. 6来评价. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明: Sec. 7是一个专门的限制和讨论部分,涵盖多个限制:只视觉假设,只鸟限制,K max = 2 K_{\max}=2 (双向分裂),公民-科学偏差,控制匹配是分类学而非生态学,以及只分化的范围. • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果只在几个数据集上或用几个运行来测试这种做法。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社区完整性的准则方面起重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 该文件提出了经验性基准,并调整了基线,没有理论结果或证据。 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 • 所有假设均应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明: 第3节和附录D全面介绍了数据集建设管道。 后骨 (DINOv1, DINOv2 有登记, GCD, SimGCD, OUN+, SELEx, SINR) 和 K-估算/集群方法在 Sec. 5 中描述,并引用了原始执行; 变压器 K-估算器架构,损失,选取器,培训时间表在附录 E 中给出 . 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是新模型(如:大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(如:有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示等). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 回答:[是] 理由说明:第3条 数据集和代码(包括施工管道和K-估算器实施)将发布 准则: 答案[n/A]意味着该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为了保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 第5节描述了骨干,地理学编码器,K-估计方法,以及集群选择;第4节给出了50/50的已知/小行星粗等级协议;第4节给出了完整的变压器架构和训练超参数(SGD有动向0.9,学习率0.1,50个纪元,5个头的综艺,\=0.3\lambda=0.3,\=0.07\tau=0.07,K max=2K_{\max}=2)在附录E中提供. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之有意义。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告的错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验的统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:理由: 报告结果来自每个精细骨干的一个单一培训种子;由于计算成本,我们没有为全骨干×\times K-估算网格进行多种子实验. 许多类别发现文件报告是以前类别发现文件的结果,没有作为培训重新实施,每种方法每个数据集需要几天时间,这取决于可用的计算。 在我们采用新的任务和数据集时,每个主干单位都需要为每个数据集和任务进行培训,限制可行的运行。 我们将在未来的修订中添加出错栏。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是好的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-相格马出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明:附录 E报道说,变压器K-估测器在大约10分钟内在全PS-SPLIT上的A6000GPU上进行列车(假设预计算后的主干功能),而PS-SPLIT-Small上的列车较少. 后骨微调计算遵循了 Sec. 5 所引用的原始出版物;所有被报道的运行都使用了单A6000 GPU. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 文件应披露整个研究项目是否比文件所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如,初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入文件)。 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 这项工作符合《新IPS道德守则》。 数据集仅取自研究级iNaturalist观测数据,其许可证允许对研究进行再分配;没有涉及人类主体;第7节讨论了在实际应用PS-SPLIT评价方法时专家的适当使用和基因确认的作用。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题: 文件是否讨论已完成的工作可能产生的积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由:第1条激励这项工作支持生物多样性监测和物种发现(积极影响)。 第7条讨论了可能的滥用:在PS-SPLIT上评价的方法应提出供下游专家审查和基因确认使用的候选人的分法,而不是用来替代分类决定,数据集继承了已知的可能影响部署的地理和分类偏差。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严格公布,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? 回答:[N/A] 说明:PS-SPLIT包括根据允许再分配研究的许可证发布的研究级公民-科学鸟类图像;其中不含个人数据、基因模型产出或滥用风险高的内容,因此不需要特别保障措施。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放有可能被滥用或双重用途的已释放模型时,应采取必要的保障措施,允许控制地使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 二. 支助 从互联网上取出的数据组可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明他们如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有者,是否适当记名,是否明确提到并适当遵守许可证和使用条件? 答复:[是] 说明: 所有被引用的资产在使用时均记为:iNaturalist研究级观测[24](仅包括其研究许可再分配的观测); v5 [3]; Quen2.5-VL-7B-指示 [2]; DINov1 [8]; DINov2 有注册号 [36,15]; SINR [14]; GCD [52]; SimGCD [55]; UNO+ [18]; SELEx [40]; CUB-200-2011 [54]; Stanford Cars [26]; FGVC Aircraft [32]. • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用了哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证的名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应当包括每项资产. 二. 支助 对于某一来源(如网站)的报废数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产被放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于受欢迎的数据集,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 他们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 二. 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,与资产一起提供的文件是否充分? 答复:[不详]理由: 这项工作不涉及人的研究,因此不需要IRB批准. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人主体的研究. • 研究对象的研究可能需要IRB批准(或同等批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在文件中明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大相径庭,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 二. 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包含任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. LLM使用宣言问题: 论文是否描述了LLMS的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作、编辑或格式化目的,而且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要申报。 回答:[是] 理由说明:Qun2.5-VL-7B-指示[2]被用作数据集构建管道第四阶段(Sec. 3,附录D)的远景-语言质量审查员;每幅图像评分七分二进制质量标准,并指定粗体姿势标签,内部组合构成一致性强制执行. 完整的即时模板见附录。 在采用基准方法时没有使用法学硕士。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Justification: The abstract and Sec. 1 state the dataset (PS-SPLIT; 79K bird images from 257 real taxonomic splits with 257 matched controls), the new task (discovery by category splitting), the four adapted GCD baselines, and the transformer K-estimator; all of these are evaluated in Sec. 6 .

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的众包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于与人类主体的众包实验和研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示和(如果适用的话)截图的全文,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing or research with human subjects. The underlying iNaturalist observations were contributed by volunteer naturalists for biodiversity science independently of and prior to this work; we use only the resulting research-grade images and associated metadata under their existing redistribution-permitting licences.
blocks.zh: 说明: 论文不涉及与人类主体的众包或研究. 基础iNaturalist观测是由生物多样性科学的志愿自然学家在这项工作之外和之前独立贡献的;我们仅根据他们现有的再分配许可使用研究级图像和相关元数据。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMS的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作、编辑或格式化目的,而且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要申报。
